div.l: That swiche a lewed mannes witte shal · pace
The wisdom of an hepe of lerned men
Of maystres hadde he no þen þries ten
Þat were of law exꝑperte and Curious
Of whiche þer was a · doseyn in þat hous
Worthi to ben Stywardes of Rente and londe
Of my lord þat is in Ingelond
To make hym lyue by his ꝓproper goode
In honour detteles but þat he were woode
Or lyue als scarsly as hym list desire
And able for to helpen al · a · Shire
In any cas þat myȝt falle or happe
And yet þis manciple sette here alle cappe
¶ The Reue was a sclender colerik man
His berd was Shaue as nygh as euer he can
Hys here was by his eres ful rounde y shorne
His toppe was dokked like a preest by forne
Ful long were his legges and ful lene
Y like a · staf þer was no calf y sene
Wel couthe kepe · a · garner or a bynne
Þer was non Auditour couth on hym wynne
Wel wiste he by the droghte ⁊and by þᵉ reyne
The ȝelding of his seede ⁊and of his greyne
His lordes shepe his nete his dayerie
His swyn his hors his stoor ⁊and his pullettrie
Was hoolly in þis Reues gouernyng
And bi his couenant ȝaf þe rekenyng
Syn þat his lord was twenty ȝere of age
Þer couthe no man bringe hym in arrerage
Þer nas baillif ne herd nor other hyne
Þat he knew his sleght and his covyne
Thei were a · drad of hym as of þᵉ dethe
His wonnyng was ful faire vppon an hethe
With grene trees shadewed was his place
He couth better þan his lord purchace
Ful riche was he a stored pⁱriuyly
His lord he couthe wel plesen Subtily
To ȝeue and lene hym of his owne gode
